title: Callback helpers
description:
Write three helpers for callback-style code. A **task** is a function that takes one error-first callback, like `cb => setTimeout(() => cb(null, 42), 10)`.

```javascript
function afterCalls(count, done) { }  // returns a function; once it has been called `count` times, done() runs (once)
function series(tasks, done) { }      // runs tasks one after another
function parallel(tasks, done) { }    // starts all tasks at once
```

- `afterCalls(0, done)` runs `done` straight away. Calls after the count is reached do nothing.
- `series` starts each task only after the one before it has called back. When all are finished it calls `done(null, results)` with the results in order. At the first error it calls `done(err)` and starts no more tasks.
- `parallel` calls `done(null, results)` with the results **in task order** (not in finishing order) when all are finished. At the first error it calls `done(err)`; later errors or results are ignored, so `done` runs only once.
- Both call `done(null, [])` for an empty list.
hints: For `series`, a function `runNext(i)` that starts task `i` and, in its callback, calls `runNext(i + 1)` keeps exactly one task running.
For `parallel`, store each result at its index `i` and count down how many are left; a `finished` flag makes sure `done` runs once.
